channel.title: Jiǎoluò Shūwū · 角落書屋
channel.description: A reading nook for Chinese language and civilisation. Characters, vocabulary, grammar, history, philosophy, and the world they shaped.

item.title: 楚辞 · Songs of Chu
item.description: The shamanistic southern voice that gave Chinese literature its second pole: visionary, romantic, and inconsolably exiled.

item.title: 古琴 · the scholar's zither
item.description: The seven-string zither Confucius played throughout his life, and the origin of 知音, the word for a person who truly understands you.

item.title: 生旦净末丑 · Role Types in Peking Opera
item.description: Five role categories, each a complete performance tradition -- voice, movement, makeup, and costume as a total semiotic system.

item.title: 鲁迅 · Lu Xun
item.description: The writer who looked at traditional Chinese society and saw cannibalism, and the complicated, unresolvable legacy he left behind.

item.title: 山水画 · landscape painting
item.description: Chinese landscape painting encodes a theory in its name: 山 (mountain, yang, permanent) and 水 (water, yin, changing) in dynamic tension. A space to inhabit in the imagination, not a view to frame.

item.title: 诗经 · Book of Songs
item.description: China oldest poetry anthology: three hundred poems that Confucius said no educated person could afford to ignore.

item.title: 书法风格 · The Five Scripts of Chinese Calligraphy
item.description: Five script styles chart two thousand years of Chinese writing, from the solemn bronze inscriptions of the Zhou to the explosive cursive of the Tang masters.

item.title: 水墨画 · Ink-Wash Painting
item.description: Where the brush meets philosophy: five tones of ink, the art of leaving space, and landscapes that are not about landscape at all.

item.title: 宋词 · Song Dynasty Lyric
item.description: The poem that sings: fixed tune patterns, named meters, and three masters who defined what the Chinese lyric could feel.

item.title: 唐诗 · Tang Poetry
item.description: Li Bai, Du Fu, and the golden age of regulated verse.

item.title: 篆刻 · Seal Carving
item.description: The art of the name: bronze to stone, dynasty to dynasty, two schools of carvers, and the small red square that authenticates everything.

item.title: 道 · way, path
item.description: The word that gave Daoism its name, and underlies every Chinese 'ism'.

item.title: 低 · low; to lower; to bow down
item.description: A person stooping: the phonetic 氐 gives the sound while the human radical supplies the posture, and together they built one of the most culturally loaded words in modern Chinese.

item.title: 佛 · Buddha, the awakened
item.description: The character that carried an entire worldview across the Silk Road: etymology, Buddhism, the 佛-family of compounds.

item.title: 感 · to feel, to resonate
item.description: Feeling, perception, gratitude, and the cosmology of sympathetic resonance.

item.title: 和 · harmony, and, with; peace
item.description: 和 carries the same concept across grammar and philosophy: grain and mouth together, the harmony of shared food and speech, a character that serves as both everyday conjunction and the Confucian ideal of a well-ordered world.

item.title: 家 · home, family
item.description: House, family, school of thought, nation (国家): the fractal of belonging.

item.title: 可 · can; may; worth; quite
item.description: A two-stroke mouth character whose ancient sense of affirming breath became the pivot of permission, capability, and worth in classical and modern Chinese.

item.title: 空 · empty, sky, void; in vain
item.description: A cave with the work of hollowing inside it. The character that names the open sky, the empty room, the wasted afternoon, and the Buddhist śūnyatā at the heart of Chan.

item.title: 快 · fast, happy
item.description: One character carries two meanings that turn out to be the same thing: speed and joy both feel like the heart cutting loose.

item.title: 龙 · dragon, the imperial symbol
item.description: China's most powerful mythic creature: benevolent, not fearsome; the emperor's emblem and the Chinese people's self-described totem.

item.title: 你 · you
item.description: The everyday second-person pronoun whose formal twin 您 embeds 心 (heart) directly into the character: address with warmth.

item.title: 其 · its, that, their
item.description: A winnowing basket that became the pronoun holding classical Chinese together: the silent 'its' behind thousands of literary phrases.

item.title: 人 · person, humanity
item.description: The character for human being, and its echo in 仁 rén, Confucian benevolence.

item.title: 山 · mountain, hill, sacred peak
item.description: Three peaks rising from the earth: the oldest pictograph and the axis of Chinese sacred geography.

item.title: 思 · to think, to miss, thought
item.description: The field of the mind above the heart: thinking as cultivation, longing as thought turned inward.

item.title: 他 · he, him; another
item.description: 他 was gender-neutral for a millennium until 她 was coined in 1917 to solve a translation problem that Classical Chinese had never needed to solve.

item.title: 天 · sky, heaven, day
item.description: Heaven as moral authority, weather, time, and the ground of 天命 the Mandate of Heaven.

item.title: 万 · ten thousand; myriad; all
item.description: 万 is the Chinese hyperbole unit. Where English reaches for millions, Chinese reaches for 万 to express the immeasurable, because the written number 10,000 originally meant scorpion.

item.title: 为 · to do; to act; for; because of
item.description: In oracle bone script, a hand leading an elephant (to guide an immense force through skillful agency), and the character at the center of the Daoist concept of non-action.
